Q: What is `<<` and `&` in yaml mean? A:

in yaml if data is like

user: &userId '123'
username: *userId

equivalent yml is

user: '123'
username: '123'

or equivalent json is

{
    "user": "123",
    "username": "123"
}

so it basically allows to reuse data, you can also try with array instead of single value like 123

try converting below yml to json using any yml to json online converter

users: &users
  k1: v1
  k2: v2
  
usernames: *users

Q: Will my Capacitor WebView social media app (offline, haptics, push notifs, camera, 4 languages) be rejected under Guideline 4.2.2? A:

Your Capacitor WebView social media app may avoid rejection under Apple App Store Guideline 4.2.2 if it provides enough native functionality and a good mobile experience. Features like offline support, haptics, push notifications, camera integration, and multilingual support help show that the app is more than just a wrapped website.

However, Apple may still reject it if:

  • It feels identical to your website

  • It lacks unique iOS features

  • The UI/UX is poor or not optimized for mobile

  • The app provides minimal functionality

To improve approval chances:

  • Add native navigation and smooth animations

  • Use device-specific features meaningfully

  • Optimize performance and offline usage

  • Make the app feel like a real mobile app, not only a WebView

So, rejection is possible, but your added native features significantly improve your chances of approval.

Q: How to get command on DSA problems A:

STOP reading full solutions so dmn quickly. Struggle of 30–45 minutes is the part that actually builds problem-solving ability, saying by exp, unless u are blessed with a micromanager in ur work — copying patterns from chatgpt won’t build those, u ask chatgpt the solutions, YES, but in parts, ask part 1, u explain what u dont understand, what u were gonna do to start solving, then chatgpt will tell u if thats right thinking or if wrong thinking for the problem u are in

Pick one topic at time, solve easy/beginner problems repeatedly, try increasing speed each interval, then write down the pattern or as they say, the intuition in your own words, ONLY u should understand and revisit those problems after a few days (2-3 times a week cycle unless its imprinted in brain) without looking through notes. That repetition is what will build command.
